Vanessa / Marissa — adding the technical details Elena asked for. Copying below as a concise Q&A so we can drop into the security questionnaire. See attachments for inventory and the deletion playbook.

1) Regions & runtime:
- Hosted (default): inference and embeddings are executed in the region selected at request time. For EU customers we route to eu-west-1 (GCP europe-west3 & AWS eu-west-1 options available per contract).
- Dedicated/Private: can be deployed to customer VPCs in any supported region (GCP/AWS/Azure).

2) Subprocessors (short list):
- Cloud compute/storage: AWS (eu-west-1, us-east-1) and GCP (europe-west3, us-central1) — used for model serving and temporary object storage.
- Persistent object storage (model artifacts, customer blobs when required): GCS / S3 depending on deployment.
- Monitoring & logs: Datadog (logs + metrics); tracing via Honeycomb in some deployments.
- Identity / auth: Okta (SAML) for enterprise customers; internal token service for API keys.
- Telemetry / usage analytics: Redshift (US region) for aggregated billing/usage; we pseudonymize and only store token counts in aggregate for hosted customers unless contractually required otherwise.

We maintain a full subprocessor inventory (attached: subprocessor-inventory-2026-07.csv) and will provide the current certs on request (SOC 2 report, ISO certs where available).

3) Cross-border transfers & legal basis:
- Contractual: we offer SCCs for controller-controller transfers and have a data processing addendum (DPA) that specifies routing controls.
- Residency routing: Hosted customers can opt into an "EU-only routing" feature where inference requests from EU tenants are pinned to EU hosts and logs containing request bodies are not replicated to US analytics clusters. This is enabled by configuration plus contractual attestation.
- For absolute guarantees (no transatlantic egress), we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments where the control plane sits in-region and no data is routed outside customer-controlled VPCs.

4) Deletion workflows & evidence:
- Soft-delete: when a customer issues an API delete, we mark records for immediate logical deletion and start a purge workflow.
- Purge pipeline: background job removes data from active stores within 24–72 hours depending on volume and region; object storage versions and backups follow a scheduled retention purge (configurable; default 30 days for soft backups, 90 days for immutable logs used for security/audit).
- Immediate purge option: for higher assurance customers (enterprise add-on), we run an expedited purge with verification logs and a signed audit record within 72 hours.
- Audit evidence: we provide a signed deletion certificate and logs (timestamps, job ids, affected object ids) and include a short SOC2 control narrative covering deletion procedures.

5) KMS & keying:
- BYOK: available for Dedicated and Private; for hosted we integrate with cloud KMS and can enable customer-managed keys for encryption-at-rest on request.

Next steps: I suggest we prepare an "EU-routing addendum" draft and a tailored deletion SLA for Pangea. I've attached the playbook and inventory for your review.

Attachments: subprocessor-inventory-2026-07.csv, deletion-playbook.md

-Karthik
Principal Infra Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Elena — great questions. Short answers up front and next steps below.

1) EU-only routing scope:
- We treat model weights and ephemeral KV cache as part of the processing path. For Hosted EU-only routing we ensure inference execution and KV cache stays on EU hosts; model artifacts cached in-region for inference. However, telemetry and aggregated billing signals may still be replicated to central analytics unless you opt-in to the addendum that disables replication. For a formal "no egress" guarantee, Dedicated/Private is the recommended path.

2) Hosted vs Dedicated for hard guarantees:
- Hosted + EU-routing addendum: provides contractual commitments and routing controls suitable for many customers; it restricts where inference and request payloads are processed but still relies on subprocessors (cloud providers) in-region. If your legal team requires proof that absolutely no data leaves the EU (including backup copies or aggregated telemetry), Dedicated/Private with in-region control plane is the option.

3) Deletion SLA for pilot:
- We can include a 72-hour purge SLA in the pilot SOW as an addendum. For the pilot we will deliver a signed deletion certificate after purge and provide job-level audit logs.

Next steps:
- I attached a short draft of the EU-routing addendum (eu-routing-addendum-draft.docx). Please review and mark any clauses you want tightened.
- Marissa will follow up with a 2-week mutual action plan: onboarding checklist, security review checkpoint, pilot start/end dates, and success criteria.

Would you like us to schedule a 30-min walkthrough tomorrow to go through the addendum and the playbook?
